result:
The proposed answer is not correct, because its own list of values contradicts the lower bound it derives.

The reduction to "every pair of vertices has at least two common neighbors" and the bound m ≥ n(1+√(8n−7))/4 are fine. The listed values do not follow from that bound.

Checking the bound directly:
- n=10: 10(1+√73)/4 ≈ 23.9, so at least 24.
- n=11: 11(1+9)/4 = 27.5, so at least 28.
- n=12: 12(1+√89)/4 ≈ 31.3, so at least 32.
- n=13: 13(1+√97)/4 ≈ 35.25, so at least 36.
- n=14: 14(1+√105)/4 ≈ 42.9, so at least 43. The solution lists S(14)=40, which is below this bound and therefore impossible.

The values for n=15 and n=16 (44 and 48) also look too small, since the bound grows like n^{3/2}. The list therefore has no consistent basis, and the sum 492 cannot be right.

VERDICT: REJECT
